the problem of automatically determining feelings, including valence, emotions and other affectual attitudes, from text.
the task of sentiment analysis, in particular, the task of detecting the affective states of a text, including its valence and the emotions it conveys.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
sentiment analysis refers to the task of determining valence, arousal, and emotions from text.
the most common sentiment analysis task is to determine valence (good–bad) from text, but there is growing interest in determining emotions, arousal, and other affect states as well.

there are many different problems in sentiment analysis, including the detection of valence, emotions and other affectual attitudes, and these problems can be addressed using different approaches, and there has been much research in this area.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the sentiment analysis is the task of automatically detecting the valence, emotions and other affectual state from text.
it has focused on developing methods for detecting affect from text and then applying those methods to a variety of applications.

the task of detecting valence and emotion is a very difficult one.
sentiment analysis is a complex task that requires a combination of linguistic, statistical, and computational techniques.
